problems: 'will now raise errors' overstates it: classes with non-Basic args only fail in some of these methods, so 'may' is the right word.
The tensor bullet describes an internal storage detail (the value of args[3]) and does not say what changed for users, which is essentially nothing visible.

The codegen bullet implies hash/sort_key/doit were broken before; sort_key and doit only became at risk because of this same PR's core change, so calling it a fix relative to the previous release is somewhat overstated.
Overall longer than needed; the important change is the core one.
Names internal-ish method details (Basic.sort_key) and leaves out the method names' code formatting; it is somewhat long for a single entry.
Leaves out the small user-visible codegen change: reshape now converts list/tuple arguments to array constructors.

structured_output.rationale: The main change for users is in core: the merged diff removes the fallbacks in Basic.xreplace, subs, replace, sort_key, doit and Expr._expand_hint that tolerated non-Basic args. That matters to downstream subclasses, and both candidates cover it correctly. Candidate B says such classes "may" now raise errors and tells authors how to fix their classes, which is accurate. Candidate A says they "will" raise errors, which overstates it. A also adds a tensor bullet that only describes how a value is stored internally (comm=None is now kept as Integer 2), which users won't notice. Its codegen bullet is reasonable, but it partly presents a problem this PR itself created as a bug fix. B is more focused and accurate, while A covers slightly more ground, so B is only slightly better.
